ogTitle: Newcastle Tile Installation — From Builder Beige to Large Format
ogDesc: The 90s gave Newcastle great houses and beige 4×4 bathrooms. We replace the second part: waterproofed, flood-tested, photographed, then tiled. 4.7★ · 119 Google reviews · (425) 595-1079.

roles.heroLead: That beige 4×4 from 1994 was never what protected your Newcastle shower — a membrane was, or nothing was. Behind great tile there's either a bonded waterproof layer or a slow $40,000 framing problem in progress. We build the layer, flood-test it for a full day, photograph everything, and then the transformation starts.
roles.trustCell: 12 years in · Bellevue based · family owned
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Newcastle, WA?
roles.costP1: Newcastle tile installation lands around $14–$26 per square foot installed, covering the tile, materials for setting, substrate prep and the labor itself — that last piece starts at $11/sq ft. Budget $3,200–$6,800 for a tub-shower surround, $900–$1,600 for a bathroom floor of about 45 sq ft, and $6,500–$14,000 for a full bathroom with its shower, floor and niche.
roles.costP2: The counterintuitive part: trading beige 4×4 for large-format porcelain doesn't multiply the price the way people fear. Labor tracks the count of cuts and grout joints, so a $12 large-format plank can actually install for less than a $4 mosaic sheet.
roles.costNote: Newcastle figures as of August 2026 — tile, materials and labor combined. Your free estimate ends with the number that actually counts, in writing.
roles.layersLead: Seven layers, in strict order from the bottom up. Every failed shower we've opened in a 90s-built home skipped one — the membrane, nearly always — and what saved a few hundred dollars then costs five figures to expose now.
roles.whyP1: Nothing about a shower leak is loud. Water gets past the grout, loads up the substrate, and two years on announces itself as a springy hallway floor or a stained ceiling downstairs. The remedy at that stage reads like a construction scope: framing, subfloor, drywall, full re-tile.
roles.whyP2: Roughly 10% of a shower's budget goes to waterproofing. Cutting that line is how a remodel becomes a rebuild.
roles.scopeIntro: Starting points only — the format you choose, the substrate we find and the layout's complexity set the final figure, written on site at no charge.
roles.cardShower: Everything the 90s builder skipped: pre-slope, bonded membrane, flood test, then the niche, the curb or curbless entry, and finally tile. You're paying for the part that vanishes behind the wall.
roles.cardFloors: Kitchens, baths, entries, mudrooms and basement levels. The subfloor gets flattened before anything else; an uncoupling membrane goes down wherever movement or radiant heat requires one.
roles.cardBacksplash: Subway to slab-look porcelain, mosaic to herringbone. Outlet openings cut precisely, edges finished, and grout chosen against your countertop — not pulled off the tile box label.
roles.cardHeated: Electric radiant mat above an uncoupling membrane, resistance-tested twice and given a circuit of its own. The one upgrade that's only rational while the floor is already torn out.
roles.cardRepair: Cracked field tile, tired grout, corners opening up. We'll tell you honestly whether repair solves it or the substrate beneath has already failed.
roles.cardDemo: The old 4×4, its thinset and backer come out under sheeting and negative air, and every bit leaves in our truck. Your garage and driveway stay exactly as we found them.
roles.materialsLead: Most dated-looking Newcastle bathrooms aren't wearing bad tile — they're wearing the wrong tile for the room. What follows is the advice we'd give beside your vanity.
roles.materialsNote: Numbers are for material before installation. We arrive with samples and a candid opinion about which are worth their premium.
roles.estIntro: The on-site arithmetic, moved online: scope, footage, format, prep. It won't replace a quote, but it will anchor your budget.
roles.daysLead: Four to six working days transforms a typical Newcastle bathroom. The quiet middle two — waterproofing and its flood test — decide whether it lasts.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Newcastle, WA?
roles.faqA1: Installed tile in Newcastle runs $14 to $26 per square foot with everything counted — tile, setting materials, prep on the substrate, labor. Labor starts at $11 per square foot on its own. Figure $3,200 to $6,800 for a standard tub-shower surround and $6,500 to $14,000 for a complete bathroom with its floor, shower and niche. Note that format outweighs unit price: mosaic sheets and oversized planks each take much more labor per square foot than ordinary 12×12 tile.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Newcastle?
roles.faqA2: Tiling a standard alcove shower in Newcastle costs $3,200 to $6,800 — demolition, the bonded waterproofing, a base or pan with pre-slope, the tile, niche and grout are all in it. Go curbless, add a bench, run stone floor-to-ceiling or build a steam shower and the number climbs. About one dollar in ten pays for waterproofing — the cheapest insurance there is against a five-figure failure.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Yes, on every job. Behind our tile goes a bonded waterproofing system rather than bare cement board: a base with pre-slope, an ANSI A118.10 membrane — sheet or liquid — brought up the walls, corners, seams and pipe penetrations all sealed, then a 24-hour flood test that we photograph before any tile is set. Tile and grout were never the waterproofing; the membrane is what keeps your framing dry.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: A Newcastle bathroom typically needs four to six working days. Demolition and dust protection open the job; substrate work and waterproofing follow, with the flood test holding water for 24 hours; setting runs one to two days; grout, silicone and trim close it out. Add a final 24 hours for the grout to cure before showering. Floors by themselves are a one-to-two-day job.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain, for anything underfoot or in the water's path — it absorbs less than 0.5% water, resists chips and carries traffic. Ceramic remains a smart, cheaper pick for walls and backsplash duty. In Newcastle remodels we put porcelain on every floor and shower floor without exception, and let ceramic or glass handle the walls.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes. Heated tile adds $11 to $16 a square foot installed with the thermostat in that price, and in a big 90s ensuite it's the difference between a bathroom that looks new and one that feels new. The mat sits over an uncoupling membrane, gets resistance-tested before and again after the tile goes down, and takes a dedicated circuit. One rule: do it while the floor is open, or skip it.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Almost always. Removal and haul-away price from $3.50 per square foot, and demo is the only real inspection your subfloor will ever get — rot, movement and finished-height problems at doorways all show up then. Tiling over the existing floor works only when it's flat, solid and firmly bonded, and even then it raises the height and conceals what we'd rather have found early.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Newcastle?
roles.faqA8: Newcastle backsplashes run $1,100 to $2,200 installed for the usual 30 square foot kitchen, covering the outlet cutouts, finished edges and grout matched to the counters. Herringbone, mosaic sheets, a framed accent behind the range and full-height slab-look porcelain price toward the top — the labor lives in the layout and the cuts.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often we can. From $8 per square foot, repair and regrout handles stained or failing grout, a cracked tile or two from impact, and shower corners that need their grout traded for silicone. When tile sounds hollow, loosens in a pattern or the wall gives under a thumb, the substrate is done and repairs buy only months. Which one you have gets said out loud before any quote is written.
roles.faqQ10: Which Newcastle neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: Homes throughout Newcastle — Hazelwood, China Creek, Newcastle Highlands, Olympus, Lake Boren, May Creek, Coalfield and up the Cougar Mountain flank — plus Newport Hills, Lakemont, Somerset, Factoria, Eastgate, Kennydale and the Renton Highlands, with Bellevue, Renton and the broader Eastside close behind.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Every tile installation is backed by OC Flooring's 2-year workmanship warranty — deliberately longer than our carpet coverage, since tile trouble tends to appear in year two, not week two. Where we install a manufacturer's full bonded waterproofing assembly, their product warranty applies too. The membrane and the flood test are photographed, so the record survives even a future home sale.
